You are the implementing engineer for Atlas ERP, in '/Users/taha/Claude projects/expremental ERP/atlas-erp' on branch feat/admin-industry (dev merged; ALL business + reporting modules complete). NO git commands. uv at ~/.local/bin/uv; run `cd backend && ~/.local/bin/uv run <cmd>`. PostgreSQL 16 at postgresql+asyncpg://atlas:atlas@localhost:55432/atlas (LOCAL — run the full pg suite).

This builds the INDUSTRY CONFIGURATION LAYER (the product spec's Phase 4): a YAML industry-template schema, a validating idempotent loader, and five shipped templates. It's the headline differentiator (Atlas's answer to SAP industry solutions).

READ FIRST (binding):
- The one-shot build spec PHASE 4 (industry configuration layer): "YAML template schema covering: terminology overrides (Patient vs Customer, Job vs Production Order), COA preset, default tax codes, UoMs, enabled/disabled modules, typed custom fields (JSONB + metadata registry so they appear in forms, grids, and the report builder), approval presets, numbering formats. Ship five meaningfully different templates (construction: job costing + AR retainage; healthcare: no manufacturing, patient/insurer fields; retail: barcode field + FIFO default; etc.). Loader validates against the schema and applies idempotently at tenant creation."
- STRUCTURE.md §1 (the canonical tree has a top-level `industry-templates/` dir with `_schema.yaml` + the five `{manufacturing,retail,professional-services,healthcare,construction}.yaml`; the loader code lives in `backend/app/modules/industry/`).
- docs/architecture.md **D-016 (custom fields owned by core)** — `core/custom_fields.py` does NOT exist yet (deferred to now). BUILD IT per D-016: `core_custom_field_defs` registry table + `validate_custom_fields()` + a JSONB/JSON `custom_fields` column helper; flat scalar keys, Decimal-as-string, portable JSON. The report builder (13.2) + forms/grids will surface custom fields via this registry. D-011 (event bus — the cross-module setup writes go via an event, see §5 below), D-012 (numbering formats configure core sequences), D-022/D-025/D-007/D-029.
- backend/app/modules/admin/ (Tenant + TenantSetting models + service — the industry loader applies to a tenant; terminology overrides + module toggles are stored as TenantSettings).
- backend/app/modules/finance/ (Account/AccountGroup, TaxCode, Currency models + their service create paths — the COA preset + tax codes + currencies are finance-owned), inventory (Uom + ItemCategory — UoMs are inventory-owned), procurement/sales (ApprovalRule/MatchTolerance — approval presets).
- backend/app/core/{models.py, db.py, tenancy.py (system_context — provisioning runs under it), events.py (run_in_uow + publish), numbering.py, rbac.py, deps.py}.
- backend/tests patterns + a tenant factory.
Latest migration = 0042. You WILL need a migration (core_custom_field_defs + any industry tables).

ADD the PyYAML dependency to backend/pyproject.toml (pyyaml) and run `~/.local/bin/uv sync` to update uv.lock (commit the lock — CI uses --frozen).

CRITICAL §5 — the cross-module setup writes: applying a template creates finance accounts/tax codes/currencies, inventory UoMs/item-categories, procurement/sales approval presets — these are OTHER modules' writes. The industry module must NOT import their services. Use the EVENT BUS provisioning pattern (consistent with the whole codebase): the industry loader, in run_in_uow under system_context, PUBLISHES `IndustryTemplateApplying` (or `TenantProvisioning`) carrying the validated, normalized template payload; each owning module registers a provisioning handler in its handlers.py that creates ITS slice idempotently (finance/handlers: COA accounts + groups + tax codes + currencies; inventory/handlers: UoMs + item categories). The CORE-owned + industry-owned slices (custom field defs via core/custom_fields, numbering-format sequences via core/numbering, terminology overrides + module toggles via admin TenantSettings) are applied directly by the industry loader (it may import core + admin... admin is a module — can industry import admin/service? admin owns Tenant/TenantSetting; the terminology/toggle settings are admin-owned. To stay §5-clean, either admin also has a provisioning handler for settings, OR TenantSetting writes go through a tenant-settings event too. SIMPLEST: industry publishes the one event; admin/finance/inventory/(procurement/sales optional) each handle their slice. The industry module itself owns only the template parsing/validation + custom-field-defs (core) + publishing.). Confirm one-directional (no module imports industry; industry imports core + reads queries + publishes the event). Document D-060 with the exact provisioning-event design + which module handles which slice.

TASK — PLAN 14.1: industry template schema + validating idempotent loader + 5 templates. Build:

1. `core/custom_fields.py` (D-016, NEW): `CustomFieldDef` model (`core_custom_field_defs`: tenant, entity_key e.g. "sales.customer"/"hr.employee", field_key, label, field_type (STRING|NUMBER|DATE|BOOL|DECIMAL), is_required, default, UNIQUE(tenant, entity_key, field_key)); a `custom_fields_column()` helper returning a JSON-variant (JSONB/JSON) Mapped column for models that opt in; `validate_custom_fields(session, tenant, entity_key, values)` validating a dict against the registry (known keys, type coercion, required present, Decimal-as-string); a `list_field_defs(entity_key)` the report builder/forms read. Keep <400. Migration adds core_custom_field_defs. (You do NOT need to retrofit custom_fields columns onto every model now — provide the helper + registry; templates register defs; document that models opt in over time. The report builder 13.2 can read the registry to expose custom columns — wiring that into the report registry is optional/documented, not required here.)
2. `industry-templates/_schema.yaml` (top-level): a JSON-Schema (expressed in YAML) defining the template structure: name, display_name, description, terminology (map of canonical term → display label, e.g. customer→Patient), chart_of_accounts (list of {code, name, type, parent_code?, cash_flow_category?}), tax_codes (list), currencies (list/default), uoms (list of {code, name}), item_categories (optional), modules (enabled/disabled map), custom_fields (list of {entity_key, field_key, label, type, required?}), approval_presets (e.g. {purchase_order_threshold, requisition_threshold}), numbering_formats (map of sequence → {prefix, padding}). The schema is the single source of truth; the loader validates every template against it.
3. `industry-templates/{manufacturing,retail,professional-services,healthcare,construction}.yaml` — FIVE MEANINGFULLY DIFFERENT templates (per the spec): 
   - manufacturing: all modules on, standard COA, production terminology, MAV costing default.
   - retail: barcode custom field on item, FIFO costing default, no manufacturing module, simple COA, "Store" terminology.
   - professional-services: projects/timesheets emphasis, no inventory manufacturing, billable-rate custom fields, "Engagement"/"Consultant" terminology.
   - healthcare: NO manufacturing, customer→Patient + a payer/insurer custom field, "Patient"/"Encounter" terminology, healthcare COA.
   - construction: job costing (projects), AR retainage (a retainage account + custom field), "Job" vs production order terminology, equipment emphasis.
   Each must validate against _schema.yaml and be genuinely distinct (different terminology, modules, COA, custom fields, costing defaults).
4. `backend/app/modules/industry/` (NEW module): `__init__.py`, `constants.py` (permissions industry.template.read/.apply; the list of shipped template names), `models.py` (if any industry-owned table — a `TenantIndustryConfig` recording which template a tenant has applied + applied_at, for idempotency + the onboarding record; OR store in TenantSetting — prefer a small industry table for the applied-template record), `schemas.py` (the parsed-template Pydantic models mirroring _schema.yaml + validation), `loader.py`/`service.py` (load_template(name) reads + validates the YAML against _schema.yaml; apply_template(session, tenant_id, name) under system_context + run_in_uow: records the applied config (idempotent — re-applying the same template is a no-op or safe upsert; applying a different one is an error or documented), publishes the provisioning event, applies core-owned slices (custom field defs, numbering formats, terminology/module-toggle TenantSettings via admin)), `events.py` (IndustryTemplateApplying), `queries.py` (get_applied_template, list_templates, terminology_for(tenant) — used by the UI later), `router.py` (GET /api/v1/industry/templates (list shipped templates + their summaries), GET /industry/templates/{name} (the parsed template), POST /industry/tenants/{tenant_id}/apply?template= OR this is wired into onboarding 14.2 — for 14.1 expose an apply endpoint guarded by industry.template.apply + system/admin). Mount.
5. The provisioning handlers: finance/handlers.py + inventory/handlers.py (+ admin if settings via handler) each get a handler subscribing to IndustryTemplateApplying, creating their slice idempotently (skip-if-exists by code). Register in app.main/bootstrap.
6. Migration 0043_industry.py (down_revision 0042): core_custom_field_defs + the industry config table + indexes. No trigger-bearing alters.
7. docs/modules/industry.md + docs/industry-templates.md: the schema, the five templates + how they differ, the loader + idempotency, the event-bus provisioning (which module applies which slice), custom fields (D-016), how to add a template. DECISIONS.md D-060 (industry layer: YAML schema + validated templates + event-bus provisioning; core/custom_fields per D-016; the per-module provisioning handlers; idempotent apply).
8. Tests: test_custom_fields.py (the registry + validate_custom_fields: known/unknown keys, type coercion, required, Decimal-as-string), test_templates_valid.py (EVERY shipped template validates against _schema.yaml + is parseable; the five are distinct — assert key differences like healthcare has no manufacturing + a patient field, retail FIFO default, construction retainage), test_apply.py (apply a template to a fresh tenant → COA accounts created (via the finance handler), UoMs created (inventory handler), custom field defs registered, terminology TenantSettings set, numbering formats applied; re-apply is idempotent (no duplicates); the whole apply is one transaction), test_industry_api.py (list/get templates, apply endpoint, RBAC, tenant isolation). Use system_context appropriately in tests (provisioning runs under it). HEED #53.

RULES: no TODO/stub/dead-file; absolute imports; ruff + pytest FULLY green SQLite (`-m "not pg and not perf"`) AND `-m pg` (reset pg schema, alembic upgrade head, run -m pg); commit uv.lock with the pyyaml dep; delete stray atlas.db; every file <400 lines; comments only non-obvious; don't print file contents. Update PROGRESS.md + tick PLAN 14.1 + DECISIONS.md D-060. Run STRUCTURE §9 self-check and report it.

Return: files created/changed, core/custom_fields design (D-016), the _schema.yaml structure + how the 5 templates differ, the loader + event-bus provisioning design (which module handles which slice) + §5/idempotency, the pyyaml dep addition, test counts (SQLite total+new, pg), migration number, §9 self-check, deviations.

# STRUCTURE.md — Folder Structure, Naming & File-Handling Protocol for Atlas ERP

Place this file at the repo root alongside CLAUDE.md and GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md, and add to CLAUDE.md: "All file creation, naming, and placement MUST follow STRUCTURE.md. Re-read it after any compaction." The rule of this document: **every file has exactly one correct home, and its name alone tells you what's inside it.** When you are unsure where something goes, the answer is in here — do not invent a new location.

# 1. Canonical Repository Tree

```
atlas-erp/
├── CLAUDE.md  PLAN.md  PROGRESS.md  DECISIONS.md
├── GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md  STRUCTURE.md
├── README.md  LICENSE  NOTICE  CONTRIBUTING.md  SECURITY.md
├── .gitignore  .env.example  docker-compose.yml  Makefile
├── .github/
│   ├── workflows/ci.yml
│   ├── PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md
│   └── ISSUE_TEMPLATE/{bug.yaml,feature.yaml}
├── docs/
│   ├── architecture.md  api.md  industry-templates.md
│   ├── research/s4hana-parity.md
│   ├── modules/            # one guide per module: finance.md, inventory.md, ...
│   └── assets/             # diagrams/screenshots referenced by docs ONLY
├── industry-templates/
│   ├── _schema.yaml        # the template JSON-Schema, single source of truth
│   └── {manufacturing,retail,professional-services,healthcare,construction}.yaml
├── backend/
│   ├── pyproject.toml  alembic.ini
│   ├── alembic/versions/
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── main.py         # app factory + router mounting, nothing else
│   │   ├── core/           # cross-cutting only — see §2
│   │   └── modules/        # business modules — see §3
│   ├── tests/              # mirrors app/ — see §6
│   └── seed.py
└── frontend/
    ├── package.json  vite.config.ts  tsconfig.json  index.html
    └── src/
        ├── main.tsx  App.tsx  router.tsx
        ├── lib/            # api client, auth, query hooks, formatters
        ├── components/     # design system, module-agnostic — see §4
        └── modules/        # one folder per ERP module, mirrors backend names
```

Nothing lives outside this tree. No `scratch/`, `tmp/`, `old/`, `backup/`, or `misc/` directories — ever. Temporary experiments happen on a branch and are deleted, not parked in the tree.

# 2. `backend/app/core/` — what belongs and what doesn't

One file per cross-cutting concern, flat, no subpackages: `config.py`, `db.py` (engine, session, tenant filter), `tenancy.py`, `auth.py`, `rbac.py`, `audit.py`, `events.py` (bus + base event class), `docflow.py`, `models.py` (Base, mixins: TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin), `schemas.py` (shared Pydantic bases, pagination envelope, error envelope), `numbering.py` (document sequences), `money.py` (Money/Quantity/Rate type decorators, quantize + largest-remainder allocate — added by D-015), `custom_fields.py` (custom-field defs registry, validation, JSON column helper — added by D-016), `exceptions.py`, `deps.py` (FastAPI dependencies).

**Litmus test:** if a file mentions a specific business concept (invoice, item, employee), it does NOT belong in `core/` — move it to its module. If two modules need the same business logic, the dependency-rule in §5 decides who owns it; `core/` is never the dumping ground.

# 3. `backend/app/modules/` — identical anatomy for every module

Module package names (fixed, never abbreviate differently elsewhere): `finance`, `inventory`, `procurement`, `sales`, `manufacturing`, `quality`, `maintenance`, `hr`, `projects`, `crm`, `reporting`, `admin`, `industry`.

Every module has exactly this internal shape — no exceptions, no creativity:

```
modules/finance/
├── __init__.py
├── models.py        # SQLAlchemy models (split into models/ package only if >600 lines: models/journal.py, models/accounts.py, each <400)
├── schemas.py       # Pydantic request/response (same split rule)
├── service.py       # ALL business logic (split rule: service/ package, one file per aggregate: service/journal.py, service/payments.py)
├── router.py        # thin HTTP layer only: parse → call service → return schema
├── events.py        # events this module PUBLISHES (definitions) 
├── handlers.py      # subscriptions to OTHER modules' events
└── constants.py     # enums, status values, magic numbers — no literals inline elsewhere
```

A new file type may not be invented per-module. If finance needs `depreciation.py`, it goes inside `service/` as `service/depreciation.py`, not as a new top-level module file.

# 4. Frontend structure

- `src/components/` is the design system: one folder per component (`DataGrid/`, `FormBuilder/`, `Kanban/`, `KpiCard/`, `DocFlowViewer/`), each containing `ComponentName.tsx`, optional `ComponentName.test.tsx`, and `index.ts` re-export. Components here know NOTHING about ERP concepts — they take data and callbacks.
- `src/modules/<module>/` mirrors backend module names exactly and contains: `pages/` (route components, named `<Entity>ListPage.tsx`, `<Entity>DetailPage.tsx`, `<Entity>FormPage.tsx`), `components/` (module-specific composites), `api.ts` (typed endpoint calls for this module only), `types.ts` (mirrors backend schemas), `hooks.ts` (TanStack Query hooks: `useJournalEntries`, `usePostJournal`).
- `src/lib/`: `apiClient.ts` (the ONLY place fetch/axios appears), `auth.ts`, `queryClient.ts`, `format.ts` (money, dates, quantities — all display formatting goes through here, never inline `toFixed`).
- No barrel-exporting whole modules into each other; cross-module UI reuse means the component was design-system material and must be promoted to `src/components/`.

# 5. Dependency Rules (what may import what)

- `core` imports nothing from `modules`. Modules import `core` freely.
- Modules never import each other's `service.py` or `models.py` directly. Cross-module effects go through the event bus (`finance/handlers.py` reacts to `inventory` events). Cross-module reads needed synchronously (e.g., sales needs an item's price) go through a small, explicit query interface the owning module exposes in `modules/<owner>/queries.py` — plus `modules/<owner>/events.py` (declarative event dataclasses only, no logic), the two files another module may import (events.py allowance added by D-011 so handlers can subscribe to typed events).
- Dependency direction for queries: finance is the bottom (everyone may use finance/queries), then inventory, then everything else. Two modules may never import each other's queries bidirectionally — if that seems needed, the shared concept is misplaced; file an issue and resolve ownership before coding.
- Frontend: `modules/*` may import `lib` and `components`; `components` and `lib` never import from `modules`.

# 6. Tests mirror source, exactly

`backend/tests/` replicates `app/` paths: code in `app/modules/finance/service/journal.py` is tested in `tests/modules/finance/test_journal.py`. Shared fixtures live in `tests/conftest.py` (db session, tenant factory, auth client) and `tests/modules/<module>/conftest.py` for module fixtures. Test names state the rule being proven: `test_journal_rejects_unbalanced_lines`, `test_posting_to_closed_period_raises`. One assertion-theme per test. Frontend tests sit beside the file they test (`DataGrid.test.tsx`). A regression test for issue #NN includes `#NN` in its docstring/comment.

# 7. Naming Conventions (single table of truth)

| Thing | Convention | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Python files/modules | snake_case, singular concern | `journal.py`, `stock_move.py` |
| Python classes | PascalCase, no abbreviations | `JournalEntry`, `StockMove`, `PurchaseOrderLine` |
| Python functions/vars | snake_case verbs for actions | `post_journal_entry()`, `reserve_stock()` |
| Pydantic schemas | Entity + suffix `Create/Update/Read/Filter` | `JournalEntryCreate`, `ItemRead` |
| DB tables | snake_case plural, module prefix | `fin_journal_entries`, `inv_stock_moves`, `sls_orders` |
| DB columns | snake_case; FKs `<entity>_id`; money pairs `amount`+`currency_code`; booleans `is_/has_` | `is_posted`, `cost_center_id` |
| Enums (Py + DB values) | Class PascalCase, values UPPER_SNAKE stored as strings | `OrderStatus.PARTIALLY_SHIPPED` |
| Alembic revisions | `NNNN_short_description` sequential | `0007_add_asset_register` |
| Domain events | PascalCase past tense, module-prefixed string key | class `SalesOrderShipped`, key `sales.order.shipped` |
| Permissions | `module.entity.action` lowercase | `finance.journal.post` |
| API routes | `/api/v1/<module>/<resource-kebab-plural>`; actions as sub-resources, never verbs in resource names | `/api/v1/finance/journal-entries/{id}/post` |
| JSON fields | snake_case (mirror backend; frontend types match, no camelCase translation layer) | `posting_date` |
| TS files | Components PascalCase.tsx, everything else camelCase.ts | `DataGrid.tsx`, `apiClient.ts` |
| TS types/interfaces | PascalCase, no `I` prefix | `JournalEntry` |
| React hooks | `use` + Entity + verb | `usePostJournalEntry` |
| CSS | Tailwind utilities only; the rare custom class kebab-case in one `index.css` | `doc-flow-edge` |
| Env vars | `ATLAS_` prefix UPPER_SNAKE | `ATLAS_DATABASE_URL` |
| Docs files | kebab-case | `industry-templates.md` |
| Branches/commits/labels | as defined in GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md | — |

Terminology lock: the same business concept uses the same word everywhere — code, DB, API, UI, docs. It is `item` (not product/article/sku interchangeably), `vendor` (not supplier), `customer`, `warehouse`, `journal entry`. Industry templates may override the *display* label, never the internal name. Record any new canonical term in DECISIONS.md the moment you coin it.

# 8. File-Handling Rules

1. **Search before create.** Before creating any file, check whether its correct home already exists (`ls`, `grep -r "class JournalEntry"`). Duplicate implementations are a `severity:major` issue.
2. **No versioned filenames.** Never `service_v2.py`, `utils_new.py`, `final_fixed.tsx`. Improving a file means editing it; git holds history.
3. **No orphan files.** Every file is imported/referenced by something or it doesn't exist. When refactoring away from a file, delete it in the same commit.
4. **Size limits.** Hard cap 400 lines per Python file and 300 per TSX component; at the cap, split along the rules in §3/§4 — never split into `part1/part2`.

1	"""Typed custom fields (D-016): the core-owned registry + validator + JSON column helper.
2	
3	A STRUCTURE §2 amendment: this flat core file is the platform-level home for tenant-defined
4	custom fields, so EVERY module (finance is the bottom of the import order) can validate a custom
5	payload without importing the industry module — the industry layer (PLAN 14.1) is the first
6	WRITER of defs, but the registry and validator are core so the dependency direction stays
7	modules -> core (D-016 ownership fix; the draft put this in modules/industry, an upward import).
8	
9	Three pieces, exactly as D-016 prescribes:
10	
11	* ``CustomFieldDef`` (``core_custom_field_defs``) — one registered field for an entity, e.g. a
12	  ``barcode`` STRING on ``inventory.item``. ``entity_key`` is the dotted module.entity string the
13	  owning module passes; ``field_key`` is a flat scalar key (``^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,49}$``).
14	  UNIQUE(tenant_id, entity_key, field_key). Soft-deactivation via ``is_active`` (never hard delete,
15	  so stored values are not orphaned).
16	
17	* ``validate_custom_fields(defs, values) -> dict`` — validate a custom_fields payload against the
18	  registered defs for ONE entity: unknown keys rejected, required enforced, each value coerced per
19	  type. The portable-JSON rules (D-015/D-016): DATE as an ISO-8601 string, DECIMAL as a STRING
20	  parsed via ``Decimal`` (never a JSON float), NUMBER an int, BOOL a bool. Flat scalars only —
21	  a dict/list value is rejected. The result is a plain JSON-portable dict the owning service
22	  stores in its ``custom_fields`` column.
23	
24	* ``custom_fields_column()`` — the ``JSON_VARIANT`` column (JSONB on PG, JSON elsewhere) an
25	  extensible entity opts into, NOT NULL defaulting to ``{}``. Custom fields are descriptive /
26	  reporting fields by design: they are invisible to DB constraints, so anything participating in a
27	  financial invariant must be a real column (rule recorded in docs/modules/industry.md).
28	
29	The CRUD service functions (``create_field_def`` / ``list_field_defs`` / ``deactivate_field_def``)
30	are the sanctioned write path — the industry template loader and a future admin endpoint both call
31	them, keeping data ownership at the platform level while templates supply content.
32	"""
33	
34	import re
35	import uuid
36	from datetime import date
37	from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation
38	from enum import StrEnum
39	from typing import Any
40	
41	import sqlalchemy as sa
42	from sqlalchemy import select
43	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
44	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
45	
46	from app.core.exceptions import ConflictError, ValidationFailedError
47	from app.core.models import (
48	    JSON_VARIANT,
49	    AuditMixin,
50	    Base,
51	    TenantMixin,
52	    TimestampMixin,
53	    UuidPKMixin,
54	    tenant_fk,
55	)
56	
57	# Flat scalar key: lowercase, starts with a letter, <=50 chars. The same shape STRUCTURE §7 uses
58	# for snake_case identifiers; enforced at def-create so report-builder JSON paths stay portable.
59	FIELD_KEY_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,49}$")
60	# entity_key is the dotted module.entity the owning module passes, e.g. "inventory.item".
61	ENTITY_KEY_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$")
62	
63	
64	class CustomFieldType(StrEnum):
65	    """The value types a custom field may hold (D-016). Stored as the UPPER value on the def row;
66	    the validator coerces a payload value to the matching Python type (DECIMAL via string, never a
67	    JSON float — consistent with D-015's no-float rule)."""
68	
69	    STRING = "STRING"
70	    NUMBER = "NUMBER"
71	    DECIMAL = "DECIMAL"
72	    BOOL = "BOOL"
73	    DATE = "DATE"
74	
75	
76	class CustomFieldDef(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
77	    """One registered custom field for an entity (D-016). The owning module reads the active defs
78	    for its ``entity_key`` and passes them to ``validate_custom_fields`` on create/update. Audited
79	    (D-010): the field registry is tenant configuration — adding/deactivating a field changes what
80	    a form and the report builder surface."""
81	
82	    __tablename__ = "core_custom_field_defs"
83	    __table_args__ = (
84	        # Explicit uq name: the D-022 convention keys on column 0 (tenant_id) only and would
85	        # collide with any other UNIQUE on this table starting with tenant_id.
86	        sa.UniqueConstraint(
87	            "tenant_id",
88	            "entity_key",
89	            "field_key",
90	            name="uq_core_custom_field_defs_tenant_id_entity_key_field_key",
91	        ),
92	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
93	        # The owning-module read path: "active defs for this entity" filters (tenant, entity_key).
94	        sa.Index(
95	            "ix_core_custom_field_defs_tenant_id_entity_key", "tenant_id", "entity_key"
96	        ),
97	    )
98	
99	    entity_key: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(80), nullable=False)
100	    field_key: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(50), nullable=False)
101	    label: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(200), nullable=False)
102	    # Stored as the CustomFieldType UPPER value (the core/finance no-sa.Enum convention).
103	    data_type: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(10), nullable=False)
104	    is_required: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
105	        sa.Boolean, nullable=False, default=False, server_default=sa.false()
106	    )
107	    is_active: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
108	        sa.Boolean, nullable=False, default=True, server_default=sa.true()
109	    )
110	    # The default value, stored portably as a STRING (rendered the same as a payload value would be
111	    # — DECIMAL/DATE as strings) and applied by the validator when the key is absent.
112	    default_value: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(500), nullable=True)
113	
114	
115	def custom_fields_column() -> Mapped[dict[str, Any]]:
116	    """A NOT-NULL JSON_VARIANT column (JSONB on PG, JSON elsewhere) for an extensible entity's
117	    custom_fields, defaulting to ``{}`` (D-016). An entity opts in by declaring
118	    ``custom_fields: Mapped[dict[str, Any]] = custom_fields_column()`` — keys are flat top-level
119	    scalars only; the owning service is the validation gate via ``validate_custom_fields``."""
120	    return mapped_column(
121	        JSON_VARIANT,
122	        nullable=False,
123	        default=dict,
124	        server_default=sa.text("'{}'"),
125	    )
126	
127	
128	def _coerce_value(definition: CustomFieldDef, raw: Any) -> Any:
129	    """Coerce one payload value to the def's type, raising ValidationFailedError on mismatch.
130	
131	    Flat scalars only — a dict/list is rejected outright (D-016: no nesting). DECIMAL is parsed
132	    from a STRING via ``Decimal`` and re-emitted as a string (never a JSON float, D-015); DATE is an
133	    ISO-8601 string validated and normalized; NUMBER is an int; BOOL a bool; STRING a str."""
134	    if isinstance(raw, (dict, list)):
135	        raise ValidationFailedError(
136	            message=f"Custom field '{definition.field_key}' must be a flat scalar value",
137	            code="custom_fields.not_scalar",
138	            details={"field": definition.field_key},
139	        )
140	    data_type = CustomFieldType(definition.data_type)
141	    try:
142	        if data_type is CustomFieldType.STRING:
143	            return str(raw)
144	        if data_type is CustomFieldType.NUMBER:
145	            # A bool is an int subclass; reject it so a NUMBER field never silently stores True.
146	            if isinstance(raw, bool):
147	                raise ValueError
148	            return int(raw)
149	        if data_type is CustomFieldType.DECIMAL:
150	            # DECIMAL MUST arrive as a string (D-015 no-float): a float is rejected, an int/str is
151	            # parsed exactly and re-emitted as the canonical string form.
152	            if isinstance(raw, float):
153	                raise ValueError
154	            return str(Decimal(str(raw)))
155	        if data_type is CustomFieldType.BOOL:
156	            if not isinstance(raw, bool):
157	                raise ValueError
158	            return raw
159	        if data_type is CustomFieldType.DATE:
160	            # Validate + normalize to ISO-8601; reject a non-string or a non-date string.
161	            return date.fromisoformat(str(raw)).isoformat()
162	    except (ValueError, TypeError, InvalidOperation) as exc:
163	        raise ValidationFailedError(
164	            message=(
165	                f"Custom field '{definition.field_key}' is not a valid {data_type.value}"
166	            ),
167	            code="custom_fields.type_mismatch",
168	            details={"field": definition.field_key, "expected": data_type.value},
169	        ) from exc
170	    raise ValidationFailedError(  # pragma: no cover - exhaustive enum, defensive
171	        message=f"Unsupported custom field type {definition.data_type}",
172	        code="custom_fields.unsupported_type",
173	    )
174	
175	
176	def validate_custom_fields(
177	    defs: list[CustomFieldDef], values: dict[str, Any] | None
178	) -> dict[str, Any]:
179	    """Validate a ``custom_fields`` payload against an entity's registered defs (D-016).
180	
181	    - Unknown keys (no active def) are REJECTED — a custom payload may only carry registered fields.
182	    - Each present value is coerced to its def's type (DECIMAL as string, DATE ISO, etc.).
183	    - A required field absent from the payload uses the def's ``default_value`` when set, else raises.
184	    - An optional field absent from the payload is simply omitted from the result.
185	
186	    Returns a fresh JSON-portable dict the owning service stores. Only ACTIVE defs are considered —
187	    callers load defs via ``list_field_defs(..., active_only=True)``."""
188	    values = values or {}
189	    by_key = {definition.field_key: definition for definition in defs}
190	    unknown = sorted(set(values) - set(by_key))
191	    if unknown:
192	        raise ValidationFailedError(
193	            message="Unknown custom field(s)",
194	            code="custom_fields.unknown_keys",
195	            details={"keys": unknown},
196	        )
197	    result: dict[str, Any] = {}
198	    for key, definition in by_key.items():
199	        if key in values and values[key] is not None:
200	            result[key] = _coerce_value(definition, values[key])
201	        elif definition.default_value is not None:
202	            result[key] = _coerce_value(definition, definition.default_value)
203	        elif definition.is_required:
204	            raise ValidationFailedError(
205	                message=f"Custom field '{key}' is required",
206	                code="custom_fields.required",
207	                details={"field": key},
208	            )
209	    return result
210	
211	
212	# --- CRUD service (the sanctioned write path: industry loader + admin endpoint) ----------------
213	
214	
215	async def list_field_defs(
216	    session: AsyncSession,
217	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
218	    entity_key: str,
219	    *,
220	    active_only: bool = True,
221	) -> list[CustomFieldDef]:
222	    """The active (or all) registered defs for an entity, ordered by field_key for stable forms
223	    and reports (D-016). Owning-module services call this with ``active_only=True`` to gate a
224	    payload."""
225	    stmt = select(CustomFieldDef).where(
226	        CustomFieldDef.tenant_id == tenant_id,
227	        CustomFieldDef.entity_key == entity_key,
228	    )
229	    if active_only:
230	        stmt = stmt.where(CustomFieldDef.is_active.is_(True))
231	    stmt = stmt.order_by(CustomFieldDef.field_key)
232	    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())
233	
234	
235	async def get_field_def(
236	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, entity_key: str, field_key: str
237	) -> CustomFieldDef | None:
238	    """One def by its natural key (tenant, entity_key, field_key); None if not registered. Used by
239	    the idempotent loader's get-or-create."""
240	    stmt = select(CustomFieldDef).where(
241	        CustomFieldDef.tenant_id == tenant_id,
242	        CustomFieldDef.entity_key == entity_key,
243	        CustomFieldDef.field_key == field_key,
244	    )
245	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
246	
247	
248	async def create_field_def(
249	    session: AsyncSession,
250	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
251	    *,
252	    entity_key: str,
253	    field_key: str,
254	    label: str,
255	    data_type: str,
256	    is_required: bool = False,
257	    default_value: str | None = None,
258	) -> CustomFieldDef:
259	    """Register a custom field (D-016). Validates the entity_key / field_key shapes and the type,
260	    then inserts; a duplicate (tenant, entity_key, field_key) raises ConflictError (the DB UNIQUE
261	    backstops). The idempotent loader calls ``ensure_field_def`` instead, which get-or-creates."""
262	    if not ENTITY_KEY_PATTERN.match(entity_key):
263	        raise ValidationFailedError(
264	            message="entity_key must be a dotted module.entity string",
265	            code="custom_fields.invalid_entity_key",
266	            details={"entity_key": entity_key},
267	        )
268	    if not FIELD_KEY_PATTERN.match(field_key):
269	        raise ValidationFailedError(
270	            message="field_key must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,49}$",
271	            code="custom_fields.invalid_field_key",
272	            details={"field_key": field_key},
273	        )
274	    # Validate the type up front so a bad data_type fails at registration, not at first payload.
275	    coerced_type = CustomFieldType(data_type)
276	    if await get_field_def(session, tenant_id, entity_key, field_key) is not None:
277	        raise ConflictError(
278	            message=f"Custom field '{field_key}' already exists for {entity_key}",
279	            code="custom_fields.duplicate",
280	            details={"entity_key": entity_key, "field_key": field_key},
281	        )
282	    definition = CustomFieldDef(
283	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
284	        entity_key=entity_key,
285	        field_key=field_key,
286	        label=label,
287	        data_type=coerced_type.value,
288	        is_required=is_required,
289	        default_value=default_value,
290	    )
291	    session.add(definition)
292	    await session.flush()
293	    return definition
294	
295	
296	async def ensure_field_def(
297	    session: AsyncSession,
298	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
299	    *,
300	    entity_key: str,
301	    field_key: str,
302	    label: str,
303	    data_type: str,
304	    is_required: bool = False,
305	    default_value: str | None = None,
306	) -> CustomFieldDef:
307	    """Idempotent get-or-create for a custom field (D-016), used by the industry template loader so
308	    re-applying a template never duplicates a def. Returns the existing row UNCHANGED if the
309	    (tenant, entity_key, field_key) is already registered, otherwise creates it."""
310	    existing = await get_field_def(session, tenant_id, entity_key, field_key)
311	    if existing is not None:

1	"""D-011 domain-event bus: collect-then-dispatch, in the SAME transaction.
2	
3	Three pieces, exactly as D-011 prescribes:
4	
5	* ``DomainEvent`` — a frozen Pydantic v2 base. Each subclass declares a ClassVar
6	  ``key`` (module-prefixed past-tense string, e.g. ``'sales.order.shipped'``) and
7	  carries ``tenant_id`` + ``occurred_at`` plus its own payload fields. Events are
8	  PLAIN DATA — no behaviour — so a publishing module's ``events.py`` is a sanctioned
9	  cross-module import (STRUCTURE §5 amendment, D-011): a subscriber in another module's
10	  ``handlers.py`` imports the typed event class without importing any logic.
11	
12	* The subscription registry — ``subscribe(key, handler)`` and the ``@on(EventClass)``
13	  decorator a module's ``handlers.py`` calls at import time; ``clear_subscriptions()``
14	  / ``subscriptions_snapshot()`` / ``restore_subscriptions()`` give the tests a clean
15	  registry per case so module-registered handlers in later phases never leak.
16	
17	* ``InProcessEventBus`` behind the ``EventBus`` Protocol, plus the single shared
18	  unit-of-work drain point ``run_in_uow``:
19	  - ``publish(session, event)`` appends to a FIFO buffer in ``session.info`` — NO
20	    immediate dispatch, so handlers observe the publisher's settled aggregate state.
21	  - ``run_in_uow(session, work)`` runs the business ``work``, then drains the buffer
22	    breadth-first (FIFO), invoking each handler with the SAME session so its writes
23	    land in the SAME transaction, THEN commits. A handler may publish further events;
24	    those are drained too, up to ``MAX_DISPATCHES_PER_UOW`` total, then ``EventCycleError``.
25	    ANY exception — business work or any handler — rolls the whole transaction back and
26	    re-raises: deliberately NO per-handler isolation (if the COGS posting fails, the
27	    goods issue must not commit). This is the load-bearing all-or-nothing invariant.
28	
29	**Handler order** is deterministic: per event key, handlers fire in registration order
30	(module import order in main.py's app factory); events fire in publish (FIFO) order.
31	
32	**Tenant context** (D-007): handlers run UNDER the trigger's already-active tenant
33	context, so their tenant-scoped reads/writes are filtered and stamped like any other
34	write. A handler doing system-level work wraps it in ``system_context()`` itself (the
35	D-007 site-4 "bus system-event replay" seam) — the bus does not change context for it.
36	
37	**Audit** (D-010): handler writes share the session, so the before_flush/after_flush
38	audit listeners capture and tenant-stamp them automatically — no extra wiring (proven
39	by tests/core/test_events.py).
40	
41	**Swap path:** the in-transaction semantics ARE the contract, expressed by the
42	``EventBus`` Protocol. A future ``TransactionalOutboxBus`` implements the same Protocol,
43	writing ``core_event_outbox`` rows in the same transaction for an external relay, with
44	zero business-logic changes. The outbox TABLE is introduced THEN (a later PLAN task),
45	not now — v1 ships only the in-process bus.
46	"""
47	
48	import uuid
49	from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
50	from datetime import UTC, datetime
51	from typing import ClassVar, Protocol, runtime_checkable
52	
53	from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
54	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
55	
56	from app.core.exceptions import AtlasError
57	
58	# Hard ceiling on handler dispatches per unit of work (D-011): handlers may publish
59	# further events, drained in the same uow, but a cycle (A -> B -> A) or a runaway fan-out
60	# would otherwise hold the transaction open forever. At the cap we raise rather than spin.
61	MAX_DISPATCHES_PER_UOW = 50
62	
63	# FIFO buffer of not-yet-dispatched events, keyed in session.info so it is per-session
64	# (per-transaction) and never shared across requests.
65	_BUFFER_KEY = "pending_events"
66	
67	
68	class EventCycleError(AtlasError):
69	    """A unit of work dispatched more than MAX_DISPATCHES_PER_UOW events — almost always
70	    a handler-publish cycle. Surfaced as a 500 (a server-side wiring fault, not client
71	    input) and, like every handler failure, rolls the whole transaction back (D-011)."""
72	
73	    def __init__(self, dispatched: int) -> None:
74	        super().__init__(
75	            code="events.cycle_detected",
76	            message=(
77	                f"Event dispatch exceeded the per-transaction cap of "
78	                f"{MAX_DISPATCHES_PER_UOW} (dispatched {dispatched}); likely a handler "
79	                "publish cycle."
80	            ),
81	            status_code=500,
82	        )
83	
84	
85	class DomainEvent(BaseModel):
86	    """Base for every domain event (D-011). Frozen + plain data, no behaviour.
87	
88	    Subclasses declare their string key and payload:
89	
90	        class SalesOrderShipped(DomainEvent):
91	            key: ClassVar[str] = "sales.order.shipped"
92	            order_id: uuid.UUID
93	
94	    ``key`` is a ClassVar (one value per event TYPE, not a per-instance field) so it is
95	    not part of the payload schema; ``tenant_id`` + ``occurred_at`` are carried on every
96	    event. ``frozen=True`` makes instances immutable — an event is a fact that happened.
97	    """
98	
99	    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)
100	
101	    # Declared on the base as a sentinel; every concrete subclass overrides it. Kept as a
102	    # ClassVar so Pydantic does not treat it as a payload field.
103	    key: ClassVar[str] = ""
104	
105	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID
106	    occurred_at: datetime = Field(default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(UTC))
107	
108	
109	# A handler is an async callable taking the shared session and the event, returning None.
110	# It runs before commit, inside the trigger's transaction and tenant context (D-011/D-007).
111	Handler = Callable[[AsyncSession, DomainEvent], Awaitable[None]]
112	
113	# Registry: event key -> handlers in registration order. Module import order (main.py's
114	# app factory) therefore fixes handler order deterministically (D-011).
115	_subscriptions: dict[str, list[Handler]] = {}
116	
117	
118	def subscribe(event_key: str, handler: Handler) -> None:
119	    """Register ``handler`` for ``event_key``. Called by a module's handlers.py at import,
120	    directly or via the ``@on`` decorator. Order of registration = dispatch order."""
121	    _subscriptions.setdefault(event_key, []).append(handler)
122	
123	
124	def on(event_type: type[DomainEvent]) -> Callable[[Handler], Handler]:
125	    """Decorator form of subscribe, keyed off the event CLASS so handlers.py stays typed:
126	
127	        @on(SalesOrderShipped)
128	        async def post_cogs(session: AsyncSession, event: SalesOrderShipped) -> None: ...
129	
130	    Returns the handler unchanged so it can still be called/tested directly."""
131	
132	    def decorator(handler: Handler) -> Handler:
133	        subscribe(event_type.key, handler)
134	        return handler
135	
136	    return decorator
137	
138	
139	def handlers_for(event_key: str) -> tuple[Handler, ...]:
140	    """Registered handlers for a key, in registration order (empty tuple if none)."""
141	    return tuple(_subscriptions.get(event_key, ()))
142	
143	
144	def clear_subscriptions() -> None:
145	    """Drop every registration. The autouse test fixture calls this so handlers a module
146	    registers at import in later phases cannot leak between tests (D-025 isolation)."""
147	    _subscriptions.clear()
148	
149	
150	def subscriptions_snapshot() -> dict[str, list[Handler]]:
151	    """Deep-ish copy of the registry for save/restore around a test that mutates it."""
152	    return {key: list(value) for key, value in _subscriptions.items()}
153	
154	
155	def restore_subscriptions(snapshot: dict[str, list[Handler]]) -> None:
156	    """Replace the registry with a previously taken snapshot."""
157	    _subscriptions.clear()
158	    _subscriptions.update({key: list(value) for key, value in snapshot.items()})
159	
160	
161	def _buffer(session: AsyncSession) -> list[DomainEvent]:
162	    return session.info.setdefault(_BUFFER_KEY, [])
163	
164	
165	@runtime_checkable
166	class EventBus(Protocol):
167	    """The swappable contract (D-011). The in-transaction semantics live in ``run_in_uow``,
168	    not here, so any implementation (in-process now, a transactional-outbox bus later)
169	    publishes the same way and business logic never changes. ``publish`` buffers; it does
170	    NOT dispatch — dispatch is owned by the single ``run_in_uow`` drain point."""
171	
172	    def publish(self, session: AsyncSession, event: DomainEvent) -> None: ...
173	
174	
175	class InProcessEventBus:
176	    """The only EventBus implementation in v1 (D-011). ``publish`` appends to the per-session
177	    FIFO buffer; the buffer is drained by ``run_in_uow`` after the business work and before
178	    commit, so handlers run synchronously in the trigger's transaction."""
179	
180	    def publish(self, session: AsyncSession, event: DomainEvent) -> None:
181	        _buffer(session).append(event)
182	
183	
184	# Module-level singleton: services import this and call ``bus.publish(session, event)``.
185	# A later outbox bus replaces THIS binding (same Protocol) and nothing else moves.
186	bus: EventBus = InProcessEventBus()
187	
188	
189	def publish(session: AsyncSession, event: DomainEvent) -> None:
190	    """Convenience free function delegating to the active bus, so callers can
191	    ``from app.core.events import publish`` without reaching for the singleton."""
192	    bus.publish(session, event)
193	
194	
195	async def _drain_and_dispatch(session: AsyncSession) -> None:
196	    """Pop buffered events FIFO and run their handlers, sharing ``session``. Handlers may
197	    publish more events (appended to the same buffer); we keep draining breadth-first up to
198	    MAX_DISPATCHES_PER_UOW total dispatches, then raise EventCycleError. A handler raising
199	    propagates — run_in_uow's caller rolls the whole transaction back (D-011: no isolation).
200	    """
201	    buffer = _buffer(session)
202	    dispatched = 0
203	    while buffer:
204	        event = buffer.pop(0)  # FIFO: oldest first
205	        for handler in handlers_for(event.key):
206	            if dispatched >= MAX_DISPATCHES_PER_UOW:
207	                raise EventCycleError(dispatched)
208	            await handler(session, event)
209	            dispatched += 1
210	    # Defensive: an event with no handler still counts toward nothing; a cap breach can
211	    # only happen above. Clearing the (now empty) key keeps session.info tidy.
212	    session.info.pop(_BUFFER_KEY, None)
213	
214	
215	async def run_in_uow(
216	    session: AsyncSession,
217	    work: Callable[[], Awaitable[None]] | Awaitable[None],
218	) -> None:
219	    """The single sanctioned unit-of-work helper (D-011). Used by the request session
220	    dependency (core/deps), by seed.py and by CLI flows, so HTTP, seed and tests get
221	    IDENTICAL event semantics.
222	
223	    Sequence: run ``work`` (the business mutation that publishes events) -> drain the
224	    buffered events FIFO and run their handlers on the SAME session (so handler effects,
225	    e.g. a COGS journal, are in the same transaction as the trigger, e.g. the stock
226	    issue) -> commit. If the business work OR any handler raises (or the cascade cap is
227	    hit), roll the WHOLE transaction back and re-raise — the trigger's own writes do not
228	    persist. Handlers run under the trigger's active tenant context (D-007); nothing here
229	    changes it.
230	
231	    ``work`` may be a coroutine object or a zero-arg callable returning an awaitable, so
232	    both ``run_in_uow(session, service_coro)`` and ``run_in_uow(session, lambda: ...)``
233	    read naturally at call sites.
234	    """
235	    try:
236	        awaitable = work() if callable(work) else work
237	        await awaitable
238	        await _drain_and_dispatch(session)
239	        await session.commit()
240	    except Exception:
241	        await session.rollback()
242	        # Drop any partially drained / leftover buffer so the next uow on this session
243	        # (tests reuse one session) starts clean.
244	        session.info.pop(_BUFFER_KEY, None)
245	        raise

125	                RolePermission(
126	                    tenant_id=tenant_id, role_id=role.id, permission_id=found[key]
127	                )
128	            )
129	        await session.flush()

133	async def assign_role(
134	    session: AsyncSession,
135	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
136	    user_id: uuid.UUID,
137	    role_id: uuid.UUID,
138	    token_version: int,
139	) -> UserRole:
140	    """Assign a role to a user and evict the cached resolution so the new permissions
141	    appear on the next request (D-009). token_version is passed so the exact cache key is
142	    invalidated. Runs under system_context for explicit tenant stamping."""
143	    assignment = UserRole(tenant_id=tenant_id, user_id=user_id, role_id=role_id)
144	    with system_context():
145	        session.add(assignment)
146	        await session.flush()
147	    invalidate(tenant_id, user_id, token_version)
148	    return assignment
149	
150	
151	async def grant_admin_role(
152	    session: AsyncSession,
153	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
154	    user_id: uuid.UUID,
155	    token_version: int = 0,
156	    role_name: str = "Administrator",
157	) -> Role:
158	    """Convenience used by tests/provisioning to make a tenant's first user a full admin
159	    (D-009): create (or reuse) the admin role with the four admin keys and assign it."""
160	    with system_context():
161	        existing = (
162	            await session.execute(
163	                select(Role).where(Role.tenant_id == tenant_id, Role.name == role_name)
164	            )
165	        ).scalar_one_or_none()
166	    role = existing or await create_role(
167	        session, tenant_id, role_name, _ADMIN_PERMISSION_KEYS, is_system=True
168	    )
169	    await assign_role(session, tenant_id, user_id, role.id, token_version)
170	    return role

13	service multiplies by is ``rate_percent / 100``.

16	code may wire only the side it is used for (a pure output VAT code needs only the payable account).
17	The calc service resolves the right account by ``TaxDirection`` and raises a clear 422 when the

21	matching how the rest of finance stores configuration; ``jurisdiction`` is a free ISO-style string
22	(e.g. ``'GB'``) for grouping/reporting, not a constrained enum. Audited (D-010): a tax code's rate

2	master, and the lot/serial instance tables.
3	
4	One file in the ``models/`` package (STRUCTURE §3: the combined models.py was split into a
5	models/ package when PLAN 5.2's warehouse/bin/move/quant tables would have pushed it over the
6	400-line cap, the finance models/ precedent). This file owns the 5.1 MASTER tables; the 5.2
7	warehouse/bin/move/quant STOCK tables live in ``models/stock.py``.
8	
9	Design decisions baked in here:
10	
11	- **Costing wiring on the category (D-020 + D-029).** ``ItemCategory`` carries the default
12	  costing method AND the three GL accounts COGS/valuation posting will need —
13	  ``inventory_account_id``, ``cogs_account_id``, ``price_difference_account_id`` — as OPAQUE
14	  ``sa.Uuid`` columns, NOT cross-module FKs (D-029): finance owns those accounts; the inventory
15	  service validates each id exists via ``finance/queries.py`` when set, and the journal-line
16	  precedent already stores finance dimension ids without an FK on a cross-module table. They are
17	  NULLABLE on the category (a SERVICE-only category needs none); a STOCKED item's category must
18	  carry them before that item can post moves — validated when moves land (5.2+), not in 5.1.
19	
20	- **costing_method on the item (D-020).** Defaulted from the category at create but STORED on the
21	  item, because the item is the costing unit and D-020 lets it change only while no stock exists.
22	
23	- **UoM convention (the chosen one of the two the task offered): per-item BASE + ALTERNATES.**

25	  ``UomConversion`` row expresses an ALTERNATE UoM for that item as ``factor_to_base`` —

1	"""D-012 gapless per-tenant document numbering.
2	
3	One half of the merged registry+numbering subsystem (the other half is core/docflow.py).
4	A document number is claimed INSIDE the business transaction that makes the document
5	permanent (drafts are numbered at posting). Because the counter increment and the
6	document insert commit or roll back together, gaplessness for committed documents falls
7	out of ACID with no burned-number reconciliation state (D-012 claim-timing rule).
8	
9	The atomic claim is a single ``UPDATE core_number_sequences SET next_value = next_value + 1
10	... RETURNING next_value`` — one portable statement that takes the row lock and reads the
11	new counter in one round trip. RETURNING is verified working on the project's aiosqlite
12	(SQLite >= 3.35; this build runs 3.53) and on Postgres, so no SELECT-then-UPDATE fallback
13	is needed (D-012 sanctioned the fallback only if RETURNING were unavailable).
14	
15	The ORM model lives HERE rather than in core/models.py: models.py is at ~273 lines and
16	adding the numbering + docflow entities would push it over the ~350-line soft cap, so the
17	D-012 entities sit in their concern files (numbering.py / docflow.py) — a placement the
18	PLAN sanctions explicitly and STRUCTURE §2 permits ("one concept per file": the sequence
19	concept lives with its claim logic). Noted in DECISIONS.md.
20	"""
21	
22	import uuid
23	from datetime import date
24	
25	import sqlalchemy as sa
26	from sqlalchemy import select
27	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
28	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

37	)

40	class NumberSequence(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
41	    """Per-tenant gapless counter for one document kind (D-012).
42	
43	    ``name`` is the namespaced sequence key (e.g. ``'finance.invoice'``); a claim formats
44	    ``{prefix}-{year?}-{padded next_value}`` (e.g. ``INV-2026-00001``). When ``year_reset``
45	    is set the running number restarts at 1 each calendar year and the year segment is
46	    rendered; ``current_year`` records which year the counter currently belongs to so the
47	    first claim of a new year resets it on demand (no rollover job, per D-012). Not
48	    AuditMixin: sequence rows are infrastructure counters mutated on every claim, not
49	    business state — auditing every increment would be noise (documented exclusion)."""
50	
51	    __tablename__ = "core_number_sequences"
52	    __table_args__ = (
53	        # One sequence per (tenant, name). Explicit name: the D-022 convention keys on
54	        # column 0 (tenant_id) only and would collide with tenant_unique() below.
55	        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "name", name="uq_core_number_sequences_tenant_id_name"),
56	        # UNIQUE(tenant_id, id) so other tenant-scoped tables could reference a sequence via
57	        # the composite-FK backstop if ever needed (D-007 item 4).
58	        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "id", name="uq_core_number_sequences_tenant_id"),
59	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
60	    )
61	
62	    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(100), nullable=False)
63	    prefix: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(20), nullable=False)
64	    padding: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(sa.Integer, nullable=False)
65	    # Next number to hand out. The atomic claim does next_value = next_value + 1 RETURNING
66	    # the post-increment value, so the FIRST claim of a sequence at next_value=1 returns 1.
67	    next_value: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(
68	        sa.Integer, nullable=False, default=1, server_default=sa.text("1")
69	    )
70	    year_reset: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
71	        sa.Boolean, nullable=False, default=False, server_default=sa.false()
72	    )
73	    # The year the running counter belongs to (NULL when year_reset is off).
74	    current_year: Mapped[int | None] = mapped_column(sa.Integer, nullable=True)

77	def _format_number(prefix: str, padding: int, value: int, year: int | None) -> str:
78	    """Render ``{prefix}-{year?}-{padded value}`` — the year segment is present only when
79	    the sequence year-resets (D-012). e.g. ('INV', 5, 1, 2026) -> 'INV-2026-00001'."""
80	    padded = str(value).zfill(padding)
81	    if year is None:
82	        return f"{prefix}-{padded}"
83	    return f"{prefix}-{year}-{padded}"
84	
85	
86	async def ensure_sequence(
87	    session: AsyncSession,
88	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
89	    name: str,
90	    prefix: str,
91	    padding: int,
92	    year_reset: bool,
93	) -> NumberSequence:
94	    """Idempotent creator for provisioning/seed (D-012: year rollover and sequence setup
95	    need no job — the row is created on demand). Returns the existing row unchanged if the
96	    (tenant, name) sequence already exists, otherwise inserts it at next_value=1.
97	
98	    A Core insert is used (not an ORM add) so the tenant_id is set explicitly and the row
99	    is not subject to ORM tenant stamping — consistent with the D-007 sanction that core/
100	    numbering writes carry tenant_id explicitly. Callers run under the target tenant context
101	    or system_context (provisioning)."""
102	    existing = (
103	        await session.execute(
104	            select(NumberSequence).where(
105	                NumberSequence.tenant_id == tenant_id, NumberSequence.name == name
106	            )
107	        )
108	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
109	    if existing is not None:
110	        return existing
111	
112	    current_year = date.today().year if year_reset else None
113	    await session.execute(
114	        sa.insert(NumberSequence.__table__).values(
115	            id=uuid.uuid4(),
116	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
117	            name=name,
118	            prefix=prefix,
119	            padding=padding,
120	            next_value=1,
121	            year_reset=year_reset,
122	            current_year=current_year,
123	        )
124	    )
125	    return (
126	        await session.execute(
127	            select(NumberSequence).where(
128	                NumberSequence.tenant_id == tenant_id, NumberSequence.name == name
129	            )
130	        )
131	    ).scalar_one()

133	
134	async def claim_number(
135	    session: AsyncSession,
136	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
137	    sequence_name: str,
138	    *,
139	    on_date: date,
140	) -> str:
141	    """Atomically claim the next number for ``sequence_name`` and return the formatted
142	    string (D-012). The claim runs in the CALLER's transaction — the number is permanent
143	    only when that transaction commits, so a rollback returns the value to the pool and the
144	    next committed claim reuses it (gaplessness for committed documents).
145	
146	    Mechanism — one portable atomic statement per claim:
147	    ``UPDATE core_number_sequences SET next_value = next_value + 1
148	      WHERE tenant_id=:t AND name=:n RETURNING next_value`` — the RETURNING value is the
149	    post-increment counter; the row lock the UPDATE takes serializes concurrent claimers so
150	    two claims can never read the same number (verified on aiosqlite >= 3.35 and Postgres).
151	
152	    Year reset (when ``year_reset``): if ``on_date.year`` differs from the stored
153	    ``current_year``, the counter is reset to 1 for the new year FIRST (a guarded UPDATE
154	    that only fires while current_year is still the old value, so a concurrent claimer that
155	    reset it already cannot double-reset), then the normal atomic increment claims 1.
156	
157	    A Core UPDATE is used (bypasses the ORM tenant filter by design — core/ numbering is a
158	    D-007 sanctioned raw-SQL site with explicit tenant_id)."""
159	    sequence = (
160	        await session.execute(
161	            select(NumberSequence).where(
162	                NumberSequence.tenant_id == tenant_id, NumberSequence.name == sequence_name
163	            )
164	        )
165	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
166	    if sequence is None:
167	        raise NotFoundError(
168	            message=f"Number sequence '{sequence_name}' is not configured for this tenant",
169	            code="core.number_sequence_missing",
170	        )
171	
172	    table = NumberSequence.__table__
173	    claim_year: int | None = None
174	    if sequence.year_reset:
175	        claim_year = on_date.year
176	        if sequence.current_year != claim_year:
177	            # Reset to 1 for the new year, guarded on the OLD current_year so a racing
178	            # claimer that already rolled the year over does not reset a second time.
179	            await session.execute(
180	                sa.update(table)
181	                .where(
182	                    table.c.tenant_id == tenant_id,
183	                    table.c.name == sequence_name,
184	                    table.c.current_year.is_not_distinct_from(sequence.current_year),
185	                )
186	                .values(next_value=1, current_year=claim_year)
187	            )
188	
189	    result = await session.execute(
190	        sa.update(table)
191	        .where(table.c.tenant_id == tenant_id, table.c.name == sequence_name)
192	        .values(next_value=table.c.next_value + 1)
193	        .returning(table.c.next_value)
194	    )
195	    next_after = result.scalar_one()
196	    claimed_value = next_after - 1
197	
198	    # The Core UPDATE changed the row out from under the loaded ORM object; expire it so its
199	    # attributes reload from the DB on next access rather than being marked dirty (which
200	    # would trigger a redundant ORM UPDATE on the next flush).
201	    formatted = _format_number(sequence.prefix, sequence.padding, claimed_value, claim_year)
202	    session.expire(sequence)
203	    return formatted

3	
4	Started as a SINGLE file (STRUCTURE §8.4: split into a constants/ package only at the 400-line

9	auto-numbered). So item/warehouse/bin MASTERS carry no gapless document number (codes, not
10	numbers). Stock MOVES (PLAN 5.2) DO register documents and claim a gapless number — the

22	class ItemType(StrEnum):

24	
25	    - STOCKED: a physical good tracked in inventory — the only type that participates in stock
26	      moves, costing and lot/serial tracking.
27	    - NON_STOCKED: a purchasable/sellable good NOT held in inventory (e.g. drop-ship, expensed
28	      supplies) — no on-hand quantity, no costing layer.
29	    - SERVICE: a non-physical line item (labour, fees) — never stocked, never tracked.
30	
31	    The service rejects tracking/costing participation for NON_STOCKED/SERVICE so the invariant
32	    "only STOCKED items have stock" holds from the masters up (validated again when moves land)."""

35	    NON_STOCKED = "NON_STOCKED"
36	    SERVICE = "SERVICE"

42	    the costing unit. The moving-average valuation table and FIFO cost layers arrive in PLAN 5.3;

58	    mode on NON_STOCKED/SERVICE items."""

75	class SerialStatus(StrEnum):
76	    """Lifecycle of a serial-number instance (parity: serial management). Like LotStatus, the
77	    table exists for 5.1 and is populated at receipt (5.2+): IN_STOCK on receipt, ISSUED when
78	    the unit leaves, BLOCKED by quality holds."""
79	
80	    IN_STOCK = "IN_STOCK"
81	    ISSUED = "ISSUED"
82	    BLOCKED = "BLOCKED"
83

85	class MoveType(StrEnum):
86	    """The kind of stock movement (PLAN 5.2). The move's QUANTITY is always positive; the TYPE
87	    decides which of from_bin/to_bin participate (the direction), so a single signed-quantity
88	    column is never needed (the journal one-side-CHECK philosophy applied to stock):
89	
90	    - RECEIPT: stock enters a bin from outside inventory (purchase receipt, opening balance,
91	      positive count adjustment). to_bin REQUIRED, from_bin must be NULL.
92	    - ISSUE: stock leaves a bin to outside inventory (goods issue, scrap, negative count).
93	      from_bin REQUIRED, to_bin must be NULL.
94	    - TRANSFER: stock moves between two bins, conserving total on-hand. BOTH bins REQUIRED and
95	      they must differ.
96	    - ADJUSTMENT: a one-sided correction not tied to a business document. EXACTLY ONE of
97	      from_bin (a decrease) / to_bin (an increase) is set — the side carries the signed intent
98	      while quantity stays positive (a decrease is from_bin-only, an increase is to_bin-only)."""
99	
100	    RECEIPT = "RECEIPT"
101	    ISSUE = "ISSUE"
102	    TRANSFER = "TRANSFER"
103	    ADJUSTMENT = "ADJUSTMENT"
104	
105	
106	class MoveStatus(StrEnum):
107	    """Lifecycle of a stock move (PLAN 5.2). Unlike journal entries (DRAFT→POSTED), a stock move
108	    is created already POSTED and is IMMUTABLE: the move ledger IS the single source of truth for
109	    quantity, so a move never has a draft phase and is never edited or deleted — corrections are
110	    REVERSING moves (an opposite move linked via docflow, the append-only ledger philosophy of
111	    D-017 applied to stock). The column exists for symmetry with the rest of the platform and to
112	    leave room for a future draft/scheduled-move lifecycle, but every move 5.2 creates is POSTED."""

14	from starlette.exceptions import HTTPException as StarletteHTTPException
15	from starlette.types import ASGIApp, Message, Receive, Scope, Send
16	
17	from app.core.audit import actor_user_id_ctx, request_id_ctx, request_ip_ctx
18	from app.core.bootstrap import mount_routers, register_event_handlers
19	from app.core.config import Settings, get_settings
20	from app.core.exceptions import AtlasError, translate_db_guard_error
21	from app.core.idempotency import REPLAYED_HEADER, IdempotencyReplay
22	from app.core.rbac import current_permissions
23	from app.core.schemas import ErrorBody, ErrorEnvelope
24	from app.core.tenancy import current_tenant_id
25	
26	logger = logging.getLogger("atlas")
27	
28	API_PREFIX = "/api/v1"
29	
30	# request_id lives in the audit module (core/audit.py owns the request-context ContextVars);
31	# re-exported under the historical name so existing callers/tests keep one import.
32	request_id_var = request_id_ctx
33	
34	
35	def _client_ip(scope: Scope, trust_proxy: bool) -> str | None:
36	    """Audited client IP (D-010). Default: the raw transport peer (scope['client']). Only
37	    when ATLAS_TRUST_PROXY is on do we honor the LEFT-MOST X-Forwarded-For hop — otherwise a
38	    client could spoof its own audited IP just by sending the header."""
39	    if trust_proxy:
40	        for raw_name, raw_value in scope.get("headers", ()):
41	            if raw_name == b"x-forwarded-for":
42	                first_hop = raw_value.decode("latin-1").split(",")[0].strip()
43	                if first_hop:
44	                    return first_hop
45	    client = scope.get("client")
46	    return client[0] if client else None
47	
48	
49	class RequestIdMiddleware:
50	    """Pure-ASGI: one uuid4-hex request id per request, exposed via ContextVar,
51	    request.state and the X-Request-ID response header.
52	
53	    It ALSO owns the D-007 tenancy-ContextVar reset, the D-009 current_permissions reset,
54	    and the D-010 audit-context (request_id, request_ip, actor_user_id) lifecycle:
55	    get_current_user sets the tenant/permissions/actor vars directly (no context manager),
56	    so this middleware captures reset tokens in a finally block — otherwise request A's
57	    context would leak into request B reusing the same worker/task. request_id and
58	    request_ip are seeded here at the edge; actor_user_id starts None (system/unauth) and is
59	    filled by get_current_user once the principal is known. All are reset on the way out, so
60	    the worker always restarts at the defaults."""
61	
62	    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp, trust_proxy: bool) -> None:
63	        self.app = app
64	        self.trust_proxy = trust_proxy
65	
66	    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
67	        if scope["type"] != "http":
68	            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
69	            return
70	        request_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
71	        scope.setdefault("state", {})["request_id"] = request_id
72	        token = request_id_var.set(request_id)
73	        ip_token = request_ip_ctx.set(_client_ip(scope, self.trust_proxy))
74	        actor_token = actor_user_id_ctx.set(None)
75	        tenant_token = current_tenant_id.set(None)
76	        permissions_token = current_permissions.set(frozenset())
77	
78	        async def send_with_request_id(message: Message) -> None:
79	            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
80	                MutableHeaders(scope=message)["X-Request-ID"] = request_id
81	            await send(message)
82	
83	        try:
84	            await self.app(scope, receive, send_with_request_id)
85	        finally:
86	            current_permissions.reset(permissions_token)
87	            current_tenant_id.reset(tenant_token)
88	            actor_user_id_ctx.reset(actor_token)
89	            request_ip_ctx.reset(ip_token)
90	            request_id_var.reset(token)
91	
92	
93	def _request_id(request: Request) -> str | None:
94	    # The ContextVar is already reset when the catch-all handler runs (Starlette's
95	    # ServerErrorMiddleware sits outside RequestIdMiddleware), hence the state fallback.
96	    return request_id_var.get() or getattr(request.state, "request_id", None)
97	
98	
99	def _error_response(
100	    request: Request,
101	    status_code: int,
102	    code: str,
103	    message: str,
104	    details: list[Any] | dict[str, Any] | None = None,
105	) -> JSONResponse:
106	    request_id = _request_id(request)
107	    envelope = ErrorEnvelope(
108	        error=ErrorBody(code=code, message=message, details=details, request_id=request_id)
109	    )
110	    # Set the header here too: 500 responses bypass RequestIdMiddleware's send wrapper.
111	    headers = {"X-Request-ID": request_id} if request_id else None
112	    return JSONResponse(status_code=status_code, content=envelope.model_dump(), headers=headers)
113	
114	
115	async def _handle_atlas_error(request: Request, exc: AtlasError) -> JSONResponse:
116	    return _error_response(request, exc.status_code, exc.code, exc.message, exc.details)
117	
118	
119	async def _handle_idempotency_replay(
120	    request: Request, exc: IdempotencyReplay
121	) -> JSONResponse:
122	    # D-013 replay short-circuit: a completed key with a matching body hash never runs the
123	    # handler. reserve() raised this carrying the stored status + body; we re-emit them verbatim
124	    # with the Idempotency-Replayed marker so the side effect cannot run twice. Registered BEFORE
125	    # the generic AtlasError handler (more specific subclass) so it wins dispatch.
126	    request_id = _request_id(request)
127	    headers = {REPLAYED_HEADER: "true"}
128	    if request_id:
129	        headers["X-Request-ID"] = request_id
130	    return JSONResponse(
131	        status_code=exc.status_code, content=exc.response_body, headers=headers
132	    )
133	
134	
135	async def _handle_http_exception(request: Request, exc: StarletteHTTPException) -> JSONResponse:
136	    code = "common.not_found" if exc.status_code == 404 else "common.http_error"
137	    return _error_response(request, exc.status_code, code, str(exc.detail))
138	
139	
140	async def _handle_validation_error(
141	    request: Request, exc: RequestValidationError
142	) -> JSONResponse:
143	    details = [
144	        {
145	            "field": ".".join(str(part) for part in err.get("loc", ())),
146	            "message": err.get("msg", ""),
147	            "type": err.get("type", ""),
148	        }
149	        for err in exc.errors()
150	    ]
151	    return _error_response(
152	        request, 422, "common.validation_error", "Request validation failed", details
153	    )
154	
155	
156	async def _handle_db_guard_error(request: Request, exc: DBAPIError) -> JSONResponse:
157	    # D-014: a DB trigger that raised an ATLAS_* token surfaces through the same envelope
158	    # as service-level checks (e.g. ATLAS_AUDIT_APPEND_ONLY -> 409 audit.append_only). A
159	    # DBAPIError WITHOUT a known token is a genuine integrity/operational fault — log it and
160	    # return the opaque 500 like any unexpected error, never leaking raw DB text.
161	    translated = translate_db_guard_error(exc)
162	    if translated is not None:
163	        return _error_response(
164	            request, translated.status_code, translated.code, translated.message
165	        )
166	    logger.exception("Database error (request_id=%s)", _request_id(request), exc_info=exc)
167	    return _error_response(request, 500, "common.internal_error", "Internal server error")
168	
169	
170	async def _handle_unexpected_error(request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:
171	    # Log with request id; never leak the traceback into the response body.
172	    logger.exception("Unhandled error (request_id=%s)", _request_id(request), exc_info=exc)
173	    return _error_response(request, 500, "common.internal_error", "Internal server error")
174	
175	
176	def create_app(settings: Settings | None = None) -> FastAPI:
177	    settings = settings or get_settings()
178	    logging.basicConfig(level=settings.log_level.upper())
179	
180	    app = FastAPI(
181	        title="Atlas ERP",
182	        version="0.1.0",
183	        openapi_url=f"{API_PREFIX}/openapi.json",
184	        docs_url=f"{API_PREFIX}/docs",
185	        redoc_url=None,
186	    )
187	
188	    app.add_middleware(
189	        CORSMiddleware,
190	        allow_origins=settings.cors_origins,
191	        allow_credentials=True,
192	        allow_methods=["*"],
193	        allow_headers=["*"],
194	    )
195	    # Response compression (PERFORMANCE §3): bodies >= 500 bytes are gzipped when the client
196	    # sends Accept-Encoding: gzip; tiny responses pass through uncompressed. Added between
197	    # CORS and RequestIdMiddleware, so the request id header is stamped outside compression.
198	    app.add_middleware(GZipMiddleware, minimum_size=500)
199	    # Added last == outermost user middleware: the request id exists for everything
200	    # below it, including CORS rejections.
201	    app.add_middleware(RequestIdMiddleware, trust_proxy=settings.trust_proxy)
202	
203	    # IdempotencyReplay is an AtlasError subclass; register it FIRST so Starlette dispatches a
204	    # replay to its verbatim-response handler before the generic envelope handler (D-013).
205	    app.add_exception_handler(IdempotencyReplay, _handle_idempotency_replay)
206	    app.add_exception_handler(AtlasError, _handle_atlas_error)
207	    app.add_exception_handler(StarletteHTTPException, _handle_http_exception)
208	    app.add_exception_handler(RequestValidationError, _handle_validation_error)
209	    # DBAPIError is more specific than Exception, so Starlette dispatches DB-guard tokens
210	    # (D-014) here before falling through to the catch-all 500 below.
211	    app.add_exception_handler(DBAPIError, _handle_db_guard_error)
212	    app.add_exception_handler(Exception, _handle_unexpected_error)
213	
214	    @app.get(f"{API_PREFIX}/health")
215	    async def health() -> dict[str, str]:
216	        return {"status": "ok", "env": settings.env}
217	
218	    # Router mounting + cross-module event-handler registration (D-011) live in core/bootstrap.py
219	    # (the two wiring blocks that grow with every module). mount_routers includes every module
220	    # router in the fixed import order; register_event_handlers subscribes the cross-module handlers
221	    # in that same deterministic order — importing each module runs its ``@on`` subscriptions.
222	    mount_routers(app)
223	    register_event_handlers()
224	
225	    return app
226	
227

1	"""App wiring: mount every module router + register the cross-module event handlers.
2	
3	A sanctioned core flat file (STRUCTURE §2 — cross-cutting app wiring): ``create_app`` in
4	``app.main`` stays focused on the app factory + middleware + exception handlers + health, and
5	delegates the two blocks that grow with every new module — the router mounting and the D-011
6	event-handler registration — to this file. Both are pure wiring with no business logic.
7	
8	``mount_routers(app)`` includes the core platform routers and every business-module router in the
9	fixed import order; ``register_event_handlers()`` subscribes the cross-module domain-event handlers
10	in the same deterministic module order (D-011).
11	"""

13	from fastapi import FastAPI
14	
15	from app.core.docflow_router import router as docflow_router
16	from app.core.jobs_router import router as jobs_router
17	from app.core.security_router import router as security_router
18	from app.modules.crm.router import router as crm_router
19	from app.modules.finance.router import router as finance_router
20	from app.modules.hr.router import router as hr_router
21	from app.modules.inventory.router import router as inventory_router

31	def mount_routers(app: FastAPI) -> None:
32	    """Include the core platform routers + every business-module router, in the fixed import order.
33	
34	    The order here is also the D-011 handler-registration order (finance, then inventory, ...) once
35	    modules publish/subscribe events — kept aligned with ``register_event_handlers`` below."""
36	    # Core platform auth endpoints (D-008): login/refresh/logout/me at /api/v1/auth.
37	    app.include_router(security_router)
